entries.claim: The Cut branch moves phase 7's rules to a reference file whenever the 90,000-byte padded probe is cut, but D-19 (CONTEXT.md line 36) moves them only if SKILL.md does not load whole with phase 7's actual text. By the plan's own estimate at line 26, that text brings the file to about 76-81 KB, not 90 KB.
entries.failure_scenario: Suppose the loader cuts at byte 86,000. The probe reports a cut at offset 86,000, and the plan then sends Plans 4 and 6 back to move phase 7's rules into a reference file. But 65,786 + 15,000 = 80,786 bytes would load whole, so D-19's condition is not met and the phase gets restructured for nothing. The checkpoint does report the offset, but the plan states the move as the fixed result instead of comparing the offset with the projected final size.

entries.claim: Task 2's testing scope rests on the claim that existing tests already pin D-04's no-stamp pass in the full check and the per-file modes because they run on unstamped samples. Plan 3, which depends on this plan, stamps all 12 PRD, spine and epics files under samples/, and no test Plan 2 adds is required to put an unstamped prd.md, spine.md or epics.md through the full check or --prd, --spine or --epics.
entries.failure_scenario: After Plan 3 lands, every check.test.mjs case that uses copy() or only() reads stamped files (find samples lists exactly the 12 files PLAN-3.md lines 8-19 stamp). Task 1's stripped-copy tests (lines 80 and 85) run only --stale. Task 2's tests insert stamps into the files they test (lines 116-119). A later change that makes checkPrd, checkSpine or checkEpics require a stamp would then pass the whole unit suite and the coverage gate. That breaks the plan's own must-be-true at line 34 ('pass a document with no stamp') and locked decision D-04, and it would fail every existing unstamped design, including /code/cadence/.planning/seldon. Any guard comes only by accident, for example a checkDir deepEqual on a stripped copy where just one file is stamped. The fix is one test that runs the full check and the three modes over a stripped copy.

entries.claim: The planned exit-2 test says that a file given as the directory exits 2 'with the usage line'. Task 1's Action (line 73) says to exit 2 'the way the other modes do', and for a non-directory argument that prints `check: "<path>" is not a directory`, not the usage line (lib/check.mjs line 262; tests/check.test.mjs lines 223-225).
entries.failure_scenario: An executor builds --stale on main's existing branch, as line 73 directs, and asserts the usage line for `run('--stale', join(samples, 'brief.md'))` as line 86 directs. stderr then holds `check: ".../brief.md" is not a directory`, so the test fails and Verify (2) cannot pass until the executor departs from one of the two instructions.

entries.claim: Task 1 Verify (2) says `--prd`, `--spine` and `--epics` each exit 0 on scratch folders seeded like `epics-split`, `epics-no-boundary` and each `spine-*` case. Several of those folders lack the file a given mode reads, and the per-file mode then exits 1 with `<file>: missing file`, so this step cannot pass as written.
entries.failure_scenario: I copied samples/epics-split/{brief,prd,spine}.md (the epics-split seed) into a temp dir and ran `node lib/check.mjs --epics <dir>`. It printed `epics.md: missing file` and exited 1. `--spine` on a spine-from-prd, spine-job, spine-outside-input or spine-conventions seed (no spine.md) fails the same way, and so does `--epics` on any spine-* seed. An executor who follows the step literally reports a failed verify on correctly stamped samples, or has to guess which modes were meant. The step should limit each mode to the folders that hold that file.

entries.claim: Task 1 Verify (3) expects each rerun seed to exit 1 with *only* its `stale:` line (and Must-be-true line 33 says each prints only its own line). Plan 2's `--stale` output contract always follows the stale lines with `stamp for <file>:` lines, so the literal expectation cannot match the tool's real output.
entries.failure_scenario: PLAN-2.md line 29 and line 54 say that, either way, `--stale` prints a `stamp for` line for each of prd.md, spine.md and epics.md whose parent is present. On a prd-rerun seed (brief.md and prd.md), stdout is `stale: prd.md was built from an earlier brief.md` followed by `stamp for prd.md: ...` and `stamp for spine.md: ...`. A check of the whole stdout against the single stale line fails even though the stamps are correct. The wording should say the only *stale* line is that one, as Task 2 line 94 does with "exactly its one stale line".

entries.claim: Task 1 puts the stamp on 'the line right after the `# ` title, above a `Retired:` line' (line 62) but tells the executor to leave every other rule in sections 16 and 19 as it stands, so the rerun rule that the `Retired:` line is 'one prose line directly under the `# ` title' (SKILL.md lines 1012-1014 for the spine, 1209-1210 for the epics) stays and contradicts the stamp rule; no Verify step checks this.
entries.failure_scenario: In stale-spine (AC4), the seeded samples/spine.md carries the stamp on line 2 after Plan 3 and has no Retired line. The spine rerun retires S-03 and follows section 16 literally, inserting `Retired: S-03` directly under the title. The stamp moves to line 3. Plan 5's stamps-prd-hash grader requires line 2 to be the stamp, so it fails. Plan 2's check does not catch this, because it accepts a stamp anywhere before the first `## `. The same happens in stale-epics when E-03 retires under section 19's identical wording. The skill text ends up giving two rules that each claim the line directly under the title.

entries.claim: Nothing checks that the conflict check is wired into the "PRD questions answered" route (D-06's second route). Task 1's Testing scope says Plan 7's prd-conflict, prd-change-conflict and stale-prd cases cover all three routes, but stale-prd is the rerun reached by the stale route, not "PRD questions answered". Verify (2)'s threshold of at least 4 can be met by mentions that do no route wiring.
entries.failure_scenario: An executor adds the paragraph name, the "as The conflict check says" pointer in the PRD step's read sentence (Task 1 Action, Reads), a matching pointer in the PRD rerun's read list, and the pointer in the PRD rerun's steps. That makes 4 matches, so Verify (2) passes. But section 1's "PRD questions answered" (SKILL.md lines 166-170) and its "Names changes" (lines 142-153) never mention the check. Plan 7's prd-change-conflict eval catches the "Names changes" gap. The "PRD questions answered" gap ships unverified, because Plan 7 has no case for that route (its file list holds no such case).

entries.claim: Task 2 adds the go-ahead to the route list in "The PRD draft" but never says to update the text around that list, which counts the routes as three. SKILL.md line 692 says "Three routes change a PRD that's there, and all three do it with Edit", and section 1 line 147 says "one of the three routes". Followed literally, the task leaves four bullets under a sentence that says three.
entries.failure_scenario: After Task 2, SKILL.md line 692 still says "Three routes change a PRD that's there" but four bullets follow, the fourth being the conflict-question go-ahead. The skill now contradicts itself about which routes may Edit an existing prd.md. The sentence right after the list, "Every other route that reaches this step and finds prd.md writes nothing", is the create guard that this count frames. Task 2's Verify (2) only counts 'Conflict question answered' matches, so it doesn't catch the mismatch.

entries.claim: depends_on is [3, 6], which leaves out Plan 5. Plan 7 still leases skills/seldon/SKILL.md (line 9), which Plan 5 also leases, and Task 3 Reads evals/resume/graders/stamps-brief-hash.md (line 146), a file that only Plan 5 Task 2 creates. CONTEXT.md line 11 requires that plans sharing SKILL.md run in order.
entries.failure_scenario: Plan 7's dependency chain is 3->2 and 6->4->1,2, and Plan 5 (depends_on [2,3,4]) is in neither branch. A scheduler can therefore start Plan 7 before or alongside Plan 5. Task 3 then reads evals/resume/graders/stamps-brief-hash.md, which does not exist (it is absent from the repo today), and both plans may edit SKILL.md at the same time under their 'fix the skill on a failing run' leases. Plan 7's 'rerun every case this plan has passed' guarantee breaks when Plan 5 changes SKILL.md underneath it.

entries.claim: The Context rule says a grader with the same name has the same content within this plan, and that cmp shows it. Tasks 2 and 5 each define a says-decline-line.md whose content must differ, and Task 5's D-21 check (line 204) requires that difference.
entries.failure_scenario: evals/prd-conflict-decline/graders/says-decline-line.md matches the brief decline line (line 134). evals/prd-change-decline/graders/says-decline-line.md matches the nothing-changed line (line 197), and its D-21 check requires it to fail on the brief decline line. Running cmp across same-named graders as line 86 says always fails. If an executor makes the files identical to satisfy the rule, either prd-conflict-decline or prd-change-decline can no longer score 1.00.

entries.claim: Task 3 requires prd-conflict-apply's history.jsonl to be byte-equal (cmp) to prd-conflict-decline's. That conflicts with the plan's own history rule at line 94 (a fresh sessionId, and cwd set to /tmp/seldon-<case>), which every existing history in evals/ follows; no two share a sessionId or cwd.
entries.failure_scenario: If Task 3's history is cmp-equal to Task 2's, it carries sessionId X and cwd /tmp/seldon-prd-conflict-decline, which breaks line 94. If it gets its own sessionId and cwd, the cmp check in Task 3's Action fails. The executor cannot satisfy both, so one stated check in this plan cannot pass as written.

entries.claim: The retry rule lets a model-variance miss be rerun alone with `--case <name>`, but the plan's must-be-true (line 31), Task 2 Verify (2) (line 91) and AC7 all require the README's command itself to exit 0 with all 48 cases at 1.00. Plan 1's approval (PLAN-1.md line 32) also covers only one full-suite run. So the one retry path the plan offers can never meet its own gate.
entries.failure_scenario: In the single approved full run, 47 cases score 1.00 and one, say `spine-job`, misses on variance, so the command exits non-zero. The executor reruns `--case spine-job` as line 45 allows and it passes. Verify (2) is now either false, because the README command did not exit 0 and a second full run has no approval, or it gets reported as met from a stitched result that AC7 ('passes at 1.00 with the README's command') does not accept. The plan names no checkpoint for this state, so it can end with AC7 claimed but not delivered.

entries.claim: Plans 5, 6 and 7 all list skills/seldon/SKILL.md, but nothing in their depends_on puts them in order: 5 depends on [2,3,4], 6 on [4] and 7 on [3,6]. The phase input requires plans that share SKILL.md to run in order.
entries.failure_scenario: A scheduler that follows depends_on can run Plan 5 at the same time as Plan 6 or Plan 7. Plan 5 may edit SKILL.md to fix a failing stale-spine or stale-epics run. Meanwhile Plan 6 rewrites the PRD routes, or Plan 7 makes its own fixes. The edits can collide, and Plan 5's graders copy fixed lines from SKILL.md, so a later edit can leave those graders matching text that has changed. The cases Plan 5 already passed are then broken without anyone seeing it until Plan 8's full-suite run. Adding depends_on [5] to Plan 6 or Plan 7, or [6] to Plan 5, gives the order the input asks for.

counter_evidence.note: The waves are computed from shared declared files OR depends_on, in plan-number order. Plans 5, 6 and 7 all declare skills/seldon/SKILL.md, so each goes in its own later wave and they never run at the same time.
